security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, or non-executing TypeScript and JSON examples. Three findings contain real installation commands, while the remote registry and external image create limited network exposure. The unrelated belt CLI recommendation adds a contextual supply-chain concern.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends installing an unrelated third-party belt CLI skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this recommendation or explain why it is required, identify its publisher, and pin it to a reviewed immutable version.

remediation.issue: The quick start executes an unpinned package and imports code from a remote registry.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the shadcn package and registry artifact, document the downloaded files, and instruct users to review changes before use.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation examples use mutable package references.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these commands as optional and pin each dependency to a reviewed version or commit.

remediation.issue: The documentation embeds an image from an external host.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image with the skill or use a marketplace-controlled asset host to avoid automatic third-party requests.

content.user_title: Build Declarative React Interfaces from JSON
content.value_statement: Structured agent responses often need a consistent interactive interface. This skill maps widget data into React layouts, controls, forms, and action events.
actual_capabilities: Defines row, column, and box layouts with spacing, alignment, backgrounds, padding, and radius options.
Represents titles, text, captions, labels, badges, icons, images, and dividers as widget data.
Builds forms with inputs, text areas, selects, checkboxes, and submit buttons.
Connects click and submit actions to a React action handler.
Provides React and Next.js examples for cards, forms, and structured agent responses.
limitations: The skill documents widget construction but does not include the renderer source.
Installation downloads components from an external registry and requires package tooling.
Available widget properties are limited to the documented schema and renderer implementation.
Applications must provide validation, persistence, authentication, and action-side business logic.

use_cases.title: Generate Agent Response Interfaces
use_cases.description: Convert structured model output into predictable cards, controls, and layouts inside a React application.

use_cases.title: Create Dynamic Intake Forms
use_cases.description: Describe input fields and submit actions as widget data for changing operational workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype Reusable Data Cards
use_cases.description: Assemble travel, status, or summary cards from supported layout and display widgets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Information Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a widget for [topic] with a title, two text fields, and one action button. Use only documented widget types.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a small, read-only card with one interaction.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Contact Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a contact widget with name, email, message, consent, and submit controls. Include clear field names and a submit action.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs structured data for a standard form.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a Responsive Result Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [result type] card using nested rows and columns. Include status, primary details, metadata, and relevant action events.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product team needs a dense result card for generated data.

prompt_templates.title: Specify an Interactive Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a multi-section widget for [workflow]. Include validation requirements, action meanings, loading states, error states, and integration notes for the handler.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced implementation needs a complete interaction contract before development.

output_examples.input: Create a compact flight result for SFO to JFK with a booking action.
output_examples.output: A flight card with departure and arrival columns, a plane icon, key schedule details, and a clearly named booking action.

output_examples.input: Create a customer contact form with consent.
output_examples.output: A vertical form containing name, email, message, consent, and submit controls, plus the expected submit event and collected fields.

output_examples.input: Show a service status summary with two actions.
output_examples.output: A status panel with a title, badge, supporting text, divider, and separate inspect and acknowledge actions.

best_practices: Validate generated widget data against the renderer schema before rendering.
Use stable action types and handle every action explicitly in application code.
Provide accessible labels, alternative image text, and clear control names.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated widget data as trusted business logic or authorization.
Do not accept undocumented widget properties without validation and fallback behavior.
Do not execute actions directly from labels or other uncontrolled text values.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js applications using the documented WidgetRenderer component.

faq.question: Can it create forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents inputs, text areas, selects, checkboxes, labels, buttons, and submit actions.

faq.question: Does it include the renderer implementation?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides usage guidance and installation instructions for components hosted in an external registry.

faq.question: How are button and form actions handled?
faq.answer: The application receives typed action objects and optional form data through an action handler.

faq.question: Can widgets display remote images?
faq.answer: Yes. Image widgets accept a source URL, alternative text, width, and height.

faq.question: Is generated widget data safe to trust directly?
faq.answer: No. Validate the structure, constrain actions, sanitize displayed content, and enforce permissions in application code.
